consensus_summary: Mainstream consensus treats the firmament primarily as the created heavenly expanse that separates the waters, establishes divine cosmic order, and visibly declares God’s glory and power, with secondary layers as throne-room boundary or solid dome.
book_summary: The firmament is the divider between the restless sea of peoples below and the gathered heavenly waters above, and the place where the ruling lights are set.
consensus_core_identification: Created expanse/vault that divides the waters and displays God’s glory and sovereign order.
book_core_identification: Divider between the restless sea of peoples (below) and gathered heavenly waters (above); locus of the ruling lights.
boundary_disagreement: Book reclassifies the lower waters specifically as the restless sea of peoples/nations (via Rev 17:15) rather than leaving them as general earthly/chaotic waters or the earthly realm at large; upper waters become ‘gathered heavenly waters’.
material_contradiction: None; the Genesis divider and lights remain intact, and the peoples reading is an added symbolic specification rather than a denial of the consensus referent.
rationale: Both cores center on the Genesis firmament as separator of waters and setting for the lights. Consensus stops at cosmic order plus glory (Ps 19 etc.); the book keeps that structure but narrows the lower-waters referent to ‘peoples’ by importing Rev 17:15 and pairs it with heavenly waters above, producing a tighter prophetic extension without replacing the central divider.
strongest_objection: Rev 17:15’s ‘waters’ are the seas on which the whore sits, not obviously identical to the lower waters divided by the Genesis firmament, so the peoples identification may over-extend the symbol.
